all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Tasquinimod, the closest structural analog sharing the N-methyl quinolin-2(1H)-one core, has excellent oral bioavailability and absorption in humans and mice, supporting F >=20%.

Doravirine, an N-methyl heteroaromatic chlorophenyl drug, has absolute F of 64% from a 100 mg tablet and modeled F of 0.82-0.895, with no significant food effect, supporting high F under the fed state.

Chlorophenyl triazolobenzodiazepine analogs show human oral F values of 44-100%, all above the 20% threshold; triazolam also shows high Caco-2 permeability (16.5 ×10^-6 cm/s), supporting the absorption component.
Trazodone, a chlorophenyl heteroaromatic lactam with a basic amine, has absolute oral F of 65-90% in humans and high F in dogs.

L4/L5 permeability records for lipophilic heteroaromatic drugs (midazolam, triazolam, etoricoxib, DMP, and other compounds) show high Caco-2 permeability; no query-specific efflux or intestinal-metabolism record affirmatively establishes F <20%.

The only low F values are rat-specific (alprazolam 4.5%, fasudil 9.46%, baclofen metabolites very low) and are contradicted by human absolute F values in the same contexts; loperamide P-gp efflux is not query-specific.
